title: Kingdom of Libya
capsule: The United Kingdom of Libya (المملكة الليبية) was proclaimed on 24 December 1951, making Libya the first country to achieve independence through a United Nations resolution. King Idris I, head of the Senussi order who had governed Cyrenaica, became the constitutional monarch of a federal state uniting Cyrenaica, Tripolitania, and the Fezzan. The discovery of major oil reserves in 1959 rapidly transformed the economy, but popular resentment of the king's close ties with Western powers and perceived corruption among the elite created conditions for Colonel Muammar Gaddafi's coup of 1 September 1969, which abolished the monarchy and proclaimed the Libyan Arab Republic.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Libya's boundaries were fixed by post-Ottoman treaties and are well documented; the internal federal provincial boundaries were established by the 1951 constitution and later changed when the federal system was abolished in 1963.
